quote: One command starts a run for one task on one GPU. The loop uses the first ten layouts of evaluation seed 0 (for Generalization tasks, five standard and five cluttered, which share tools) and proceeds layout by layout. The acting agent attempts the layout with the current tools. On success, the optimizer agent reads the trajectory and adds a short entry to playbook.md on which tools worked and why. On failure, it reads the command log, the camera frames of every command and the current tool code. It writes a diagnosis to skill.md and adds or fixes a tool. A delivery check then verifies that files are complete, tools load, and the interface text names neither the task nor its objects; if the check fails the edit is reverted. The simulator is restarted and the same layout is attempted again, up to five edits per layout. After the tenth layout the optimizer consolidates its notes, the tool set is frozen and tested once more with no optimizer, on the ten development layouts and on ten new layouts ( Section 4.1 ).
supports_zh: 失败触发读轨迹、诊断、改工具；交付检查失败回滚；工具冻结后用于新布局。

quote: Both agents run GPT-6-Astra. The optimizer writes only under tasks/ ⟨ \langle task ⟩ \rangle / and cannot touch the harness, the manual or the shared pool. The RGB tools come from one run per task with a development budget of 12 hours. Each run started from the tools of our earlier runs with depth, and for 25 tasks the optimizer also read a short note on what the checker requires, written from the public task definitions; the acting agent never sees the notes ( Appendix D ).
supports_zh: 优化器仅能改任务工具，不能改共享Harness；不得将组件更新说成全框架更新。

quote: The RGB tools grew out of two earlier lines. The first used rendered depth. Its fully automatic first round, on all 42 tasks, reached 38.0% on the leaderboard’s metric. A second round gave the optimizer short notes on what the checker requires for the tasks where it lagged most ( Table 7 ), and a team member rebuilt the tool of build tower by hand. Its current tools reach 48.8% ( Table 1 ). The second line kept these tools but replaced rendered depth with Depth Anything V2 Base [ 65 ] inside the server. We developed 22 tasks again for up to 24 hours each, kept the new tools of ten of them, and the line reached 29.6%. The RGB runs started from the tools of the second line.
supports_zh: 旧分支也有人类与旧工具输入，不是纯粹从零无人参与。

quote: The notes of the first line stayed in the task directories and were given to the optimizer in every round. By the time of the RGB runs, 25 tasks had such a note, written by us from the public task definitions. They state the success conditions and, for some tasks, object sizes or target positions from these definitions. The acting agent never sees them. Nine tasks also started from RGB tools written by a colleague with another coding agent.
supports_zh: 旧版本已说明任务定义笔记、同事工具种子与固定几何审计；保留历史反证。

quote: HexaShell separates what is shared from what is specific. A single robot API, agent loop and sandbox, written and tested once, serve every task in every setting, and their perception and motion tools are general enough that the agent rarely needs more ( Sections 2.1 and 2.2 ). Setting-specific input is limited to an adapter below the API and the text of the prompt ( Section 2.3 ); task-specific input is limited to an optional skill, about a page of guidance on the success condition, the steps that work and a few parameters from earlier runs ( Section 2.4 ). Section 3 evaluates the general tools alone, the transfer of the harness across settings, and the effect of the skills.
supports_zh: API、agent loop和sandbox是通用固定工程；不能因有Harness名义称为自演化。

quote: 2.4 Task skills A skill is a Markdown file for one task: about a page of guidance, not a program. Every skill on LIBERO-PRO, RoboCasa365 and RoboTwin 2.0 has five sections: • Judging : what counts as done, as earlier runs showed it, with no internal threshold of the checker; • Flow : the steps that worked, in order, with the calls to use; • Verified parameters : numbers measured in earlier runs, such as grasp heights, offsets and openings; • Common failures and fixes : what went wrong and what to do instead; • Typical step costs : how many steps each phase took, so that the agent can plan its budget. RoboDojo skills also have a section of final checks and, for the twelve Generalization tasks, one on clutter. Appendix H shows three skills in full. Skills are drafted by an analysis agent, which reads the records of earlier runs of a group of related tasks, including every cell, output and image, and marks the evidence behind each claim; a person reviews every draft. A skill may contain only what the agent could observe: no positions read from the simulator, no internal names and no checker thresholds, a constraint enforced by a checking script. The median skill has 39 to 61 lines, depending on the benchmark, and only three of the 205 skills contain code ( Section E.6 ).
supports_zh: 技能包含事实与参数，也含按序工具调用、失败处理和预算策略，不能统一归为裸经验条目。

quote: Skills are drafted by an analysis agent, which reads the records of earlier runs of a group of related tasks, including every cell, output and image, and marks the evidence behind each claim; a person reviews every draft. A skill may contain only what the agent could observe: no positions read from the simulator, no internal names and no checker thresholds, a constraint enforced by a checking script. The median skill has 39 to 61 lines, depending on the benchmark, and only three of the 205 skills contain code ( Section E.6 ).
supports_zh: 分析Agent从每个cell、输出、图像起草，每份草稿由人审；脚本做可观察性与格式检查。

quote: Skills are written from the records of earlier runs and, where HexaShell-TaskTools had tools for a task, from what those tools had shown. Each claim carries its evidence. On the three newer benchmarks this is the number of episodes it was seen in, such as “(7 eps)”, or a mark for a probe, a scripted test, a HexaShell-TaskTools tool, or “untested”. RoboDojo skills name the development round and layouts instead, such as “R0 8/8” or “(l0)”. A checking script enforces the rules of Section 2.4 together with the format. On the three newer benchmarks a skill has at most 45 lines of 100 characters. On RoboTwin 2.0 the skills use only the instruction wording of the learning runs, never the unseen wording of the test. The RoboDojo skills went through four versions during the development rounds on layouts 0–9 of seed 0. The skills cite only learning and validation episodes.
supports_zh: RoboDojo技能历经四版、只引用学习和验证episode；有反馈驱动跨轮保留，不只是一次静态模板。

quote: Table 16 divides the characters of each benchmark’s skills among their sections and counts the evidence marks as they are written in the skills. The largest part of every benchmark’s skills is the flow, 31 to 56% of the characters. Common failures with their fixes come next (15–23%), then what counts as done (9–21%), verified numbers (10–15%) and step costs (5–9%). The skills of the three newer benchmarks cite their evidence: 932 to 1,136 episode counts per benchmark, such as “(7 eps)”, which name 5,928 to 7,776 episodes in all; the episodes are summed over all marks, so one episode can count several times. LIBERO-PRO’s skills also cite 513 probes, short tests run for a skill, and RoboCasa365’s 6 probes, 50 scripted tests and 140 results of HexaShell-TaskTools’s tools. The RoboDojo skills cite development rounds and layouts instead, such as “R0 8/8” or “(l0)”. Claims without evidence are marked as untested, 10 to 71 per benchmark. On RoboDojo 19% of the characters are code, nearly all of it the reference code of insert key and fill egg holder.
supports_zh: Flow与失败修正规则占技能主要内容；仍有未验证条目和重复episode引证，不视为全部独立证据。

quote: Prompts, tools and skills were built on the development episodes of Table 7 , not on the test episodes. On RoboDojo these were five rounds on seed 0 and layouts 0–9 (R0–R4); on RoboCasa365, learning seeds 0–9 and validation seeds 10–19 of the pretrain50 split; on LIBERO-PRO, learning states 0–9 and validation states 10–19; and on RoboTwin 2.0, ten learning and ten validation seeds per task below 100000. Between R0 and R1, which added the first skills and a new motion planner, successes on the 34 tasks outside Open rose from 173 to 251 of 340, and R4 solved 330 of 422 episodes of all 42 tasks. The test episodes differ from the development ones in their layouts and seeds (RoboDojo), seeds and kitchens (RoboCasa365), initial states (LIBERO-PRO), and seeds and instruction templates (RoboTwin 2.0). RoboDojo’s layouts 10–19 are public, while its official evaluation uses layouts that are not. HexaShell has been submitted to RoboDojo’s official evaluation.
supports_zh: 开发轮次与测试布局/种子等不同；R0到R1同时变更运动规划器，不能把差值全归给技能。

quote: Our results come from our own evaluations on public test episodes, with fewer episodes than the official protocols. A skill requires runs of its task, so a new task starts at the level of the general components, and we have not measured how few runs suffice. We have not yet quantified the contribution of SAM 3 and the geometry by switching them off. Slips of held objects remain the most common failure, and the real robots run without SAM 3, with few episodes so far.
supports_zh: 作者明确新任务仍从通用组件起步；不能声称同一技能跨新任务类别迁移。

quote: In plug in charger, the agent must insert the two prongs of a charger lying on the table into a power strip. Without a skill it found, grasped and carried the charger, yet passed only 9 of 30 episodes; in its own words, the charger “did not remain seated and tipped onto the table beside the strip”. The skill, 61 lines without code, states what the development runs had shown: insert with a level hand at the strip’s grasp yaw ± 90 ∘ \pm 90^{\circ} ; seat the grasp point 1.8–2 cm above the strip’s measured top, asking for 0.4 cm lower because a held load stops short; let go only at the seat (0 of 8 counted otherwise); and, since a charger tilted by 3 ∘ 3^{\circ} or more never went in (0 of 13), check both arms with dry_run and let the other arm move the strip if neither can insert level. With the skill the task passes 28 of 30 ( Fig. 7 , top). None of these facts is visible in the images or stated on the card. Press by number ( Fig. 7 , bottom) illustrates a different kind of fix: a counting rule that keeps the agent from pressing again to make sure ( Section I.3 ). Section C.1 follows six more tasks through one test episode each, without and with the skill. Skills also make episodes cheaper, reducing the turns by 17%, the steps by 19% and the reasoning tokens by 44% ( Section I.5 ).
supports_zh: 插充电器技能直接规定动作顺序、测量后相对偏移、dry-run双臂选择及失败替代路线。

quote: With the skill the task passed all 30 episodes at both efforts. The failures without the skill came from counting, and the skill’s rule addresses them: count every press once, and never press again to be sure. At effort xhigh, however, the agent without a skill also passed 29 of 30, so there the higher effort did most of what the rule does. The skill still shortens the episodes: at xhigh a success took a median of 162 steps with it and 247 without (153 and 265 at high). Appendix J shows one episode with the skill at effort high, with five cells, 109 steps and 86 seconds. The skill’s only code is the loop above, which the agent would otherwise write itself.
supports_zh: 按数按键把失败教训变成每次只计一次、禁止再次确认按压的执行规则。

quote: Knowledge that a general harness lacks about a task can be supplied either as brief guidance, as in HexaShell, or as an elaborate task-specific toolset. HexaShell-TaskTools, an earlier version of our agent listed as HexaShell-Preview on the RoboDojo leaderboard, takes the latter approach. An acting agent (the Codex command-line agent with GPT-6-Astra) drives the robot through a command line. After each failed episode, an optimizer agent of the same model writes or repairs the task’s tools, with their tests, and the same layout is tried again. Each task was developed for up to 12 hours on the first ten layouts of seed 0, the same development layouts that HexaShell used. The 769 optimizer rounds left 327 task commands in about 78,000 lines of Python, which were then frozen. In RoboDojo’s official evaluation, on a hidden seed with 50 episodes per task, they reach a success rate of 46.9 and a score of 53.2. Table 6 sets this official result against our two test runs of Table 3 , overall and per dimension, with the Open tasks counted as in Table 3 .
supports_zh: TaskTools历史优化器经769轮留下327命令约78000行；这些数字属于旧代码分支。

quote: The resulting code is large and generalizes poorly. Re-run after freezing, the tools pass only 152 of the 420 development episodes on which they were built (36%). An audit further found object sizes copied from the scenes into the tools of seven tasks, a shortcut that a measurement within the episode should replace. HexaShell, by contrast, keeps no tools for any task. Its 34 RoboDojo skills are plain text, about 2,700 lines in total or about a page per task, each of which a person can read and verify; only three contain code ( Section E.6 ).
supports_zh: 冻结后仅通过152/420开发回放、七任务有从场景复制对象大小的捷径；不是新技能分支的通过率。

quote: Brief guidance proves more effective than a large toolset. Even without skills, HexaShell outperforms HexaShell-TaskTools in every dimension. With skills, it reaches a success rate of 85.0 and a score of 88.8, and the gap is largest precisely where per-task code was expected to help most: Precision and Long-Horizon, 86.3 and 82.9 against 32.0 and 31.5. Although the official evaluation and our test runs use different episodes, the ranking also holds on public episodes: on 420 episodes of seed 0, with the same layouts outside Generalization, the frozen tools of HexaShell-TaskTools pass 157, HexaShell 284 without skills and 351 with them. Since the two versions also differ in the loop, perception, motion and prompt, this comparison establishes that general tools with short skills outperform tools written for each task, but not which change matters most. A paired comparison isolates the skills: of the 1,020 RoboDojo episodes outside Open, 234 succeed only with skills and 37 only without ( p < 0.001 p<0.001 ; Appendix D ).
supports_zh: 新旧分支还改变loop、感知、运动、prompt，跨分支成绩不能独立归因于技能。

quote: Coding agents read a repository, run its tests and fix the code [ 18 , 41 , 82 , 78 ] , and Reflexion [ 68 ] keeps verbal lessons from failed attempts. Voyager [ 73 ] grows a library of code skills while playing Minecraft. Toolformer [ 67 ] learns when to call tools, LATM [ 13 ] and CRAFT [ 85 ] have language models write and retrieve tools, and self-improving systems modify their own programs and retain the changes that raise a score [ 86 , 60 , 52 ] . In robotics, recent harnesses let coding agents program, test and refine robot skills [ 26 , 53 , 80 , 74 , 25 , 72 , 17 , 87 ] , some starting from a few human demonstrations [ 51 , 42 ] . URAI pairs a programming agent that writes motion tools with an execution agent that calls them [ 32 ] . EmbodiedEvo turns physical feedback into code skills and diagnostic lessons [ 45 ] , MEMENTO evolves code policies with a memory of past programs [ 71 ] , and Gao et al . [ 31 ] treat tools, traces and memory as code that a physical coding agent revises. In most of these systems, what is retained for a task is code, as in HexaShell-TaskTools, an earlier version of our agent that wrote and repaired tools for each task ( Section 3.4 ). In HexaShell the code is general and fixed, and what is retained for a task is only a short, reviewed skill in natural language. In this respect it is closer to Reflexion’s verbal lessons than to a skill library.
supports_zh: 作者将保留对象称为reviewed natural-language skill并类比Reflexion，应保留这一经验属性边界。

quote: Since the two runs of each episode differ only in the skill, the success with it shows that the agent could perceive and handle the objects of that episode. What it lacked without the skill was a fact about the task, which the skill supplied in a few lines. The facts are of the three kinds named in Fig. 6 . Three are success conditions that the card leaves open: which tile to place and where it stands (make kong), which end of each pen goes up (fill pen holder) and when a moved box still counts as aligned (pack objects into box). One is a parameter that only contact reveals: a turn that pushes the nut down, with the measured heights that tell a seated nut from one on the tip (fasten screws). Two concern the ordering of steps: each pillar level is built from one pillar of each side (build tower), and the arm and pitch of the whole carry are settled by dry runs before the first slice is grasped (make toast). In five of the episodes, the agent without the skill spent its remaining steps on a repair that the skill rules out: straightening the box, turning the nut back and forth, moving the discard, taking apart the top of a tower whose lower pair could not be credited, and recovering a fallen slice while a third one took its slot. Each of these facts came from development runs in which an attempt succeeded or failed for a reason that the card does not state. The skills leave other failures in place. With the skill, fill pen holder still fails 14 times, each time with a highlighter that would not stay in the held holder; make toast fails 9 times, each time after a slice slipped; and the one failure of build tower stopped at a finished tower for a reason the record does not show. The make-toast skill also cost episodes: in three cluttered layouts, the agent with it carried each slice with one arm at a pitch of 0 ∘ 0^{\circ} to 30 ∘ 30^{\circ} and lost one, whereas the agent without it handed the slices between the arms, which the skill advises against, and succeeded.
supports_zh: 行为规则也会在cluttered布局限制有效策略，技能有损失，不能写成单调改进。

quote: Appendix D Paired comparisons Table 14 : Paired comparisons. Each row runs the same episodes twice and changes one thing. Before and after: successes. Lost and gained: episodes that succeed only before or only after. p p : exact two-sided sign test on these episodes. In-sample: the change was written from the records of the same episodes, so its gain is optimistic. a Insert key is left out, since its skill differed between the two runs; at xhigh, sweep blocks and fill egg holder used later versions of their skills. b The run without skills also kept up to 50 pictures in the conversation instead of 20. c Insert key, make kong and store laptop and headphones, which passed none of their 30 episodes in an earlier run without skills, were not run again before the change and count as 0; after it they pass none either. Change Benchmark, setting Episodes Before After Lost Gained p p Skills Skills on RoboDojo, 34 tasks 1,020 667 864 37 234 < < 0.001 Skills on RoboCasa365, 50 tasks b 1,500 890 1,284 72 466 < < 0.001 Skills on LIBERO-PRO, 54 tasks, validation states 540 252 531 7 286 < < 0.001 Skills v1 → \to v2 (in-sample) RoboTwin 2.0, 15 tasks, validation seeds 150 126 142 7 23 0.005 Reasoning effort High → \to xhigh RoboDojo, no skills, 34 tasks c 1,020 615 667 68 120 < < 0.001 High → \to xhigh RoboDojo, skills, 33 tasks a 990 782 844 54 116 < < 0.001 High → \to xhigh RoboCasa365, skills, 50 tasks 1,500 1,229 1,284 81 136 < < 0.001 Harness Picture window 20/14 → \to 90/60 RoboDojo, no skills, 38 tasks 1,140 805 818 96 109 0.40 Remembered findings (Env_ICL) on RoboDojo, skills, 42 tasks 1,260 973 981 91 99 0.61 Re-measure after carrying RoboDojo, no skills, 38 tasks 1,140 807 805 108 106 0.95 Table 14 collects the paired comparisons we ran. Each changes one thing and runs the same episodes twice. The skills have the largest effect we measured ( Section 3.4 ). At effort high on RoboDojo they gain 228 episodes and lose 60, from 615 to 783 successes. The 54 LIBERO-PRO tasks of the control are those that got a skill in the first round, 54 of the 65 tasks that failed at least one learning episode. Raising the reasoning effort from high to xhigh helps in all three comparisons we ran. On RoboDojo without skills it gains 120 episodes and loses 68, and with skills, on 33 tasks, it gains 116 and loses 54. On RoboCasa365 with skills it gains 136 and loses 81. All three are significant ( p < 0.001 p<0.001 ). Insert key is left out of the second comparison because its skill differed between the two runs. For the same turn of the same episode it costs 2.4 to 3.3 times the reasoning tokens ( Section I.5 ). Three changes to the harness, each compared at effort high, made no measurable difference. Keeping up to 90 pictures in the conversation instead of 20 gained 109 episodes and lost 96. Remembered findings (Env_ICL), an object beside robot that records what earlier cells found and what went wrong, gained 99 and lost 91. Measuring an object again after it is put down, where the hand put it, gained 106 and lost 108. In each of these comparisons 15 to 19% of the episodes changed outcome, in both directions alike. Two runs of the same episodes therefore differ in many episodes even when nothing that matters has changed, and a comparison of totals over a few hundred episodes cannot separate a small effect from this noise. Env_ICL is off in every run of Tables 3 , 4 , 8 and 9 . On the code of round R0 and its 420 development episodes, we compared our system prompt with one taken from the manual of another open agent framework. Ours solved 223 episodes and the other 198, so we kept ours.
supports_zh: RoboTwin技能v1→v2比较明确in-sample；Env_ICL是另一记忆机制且主实验关闭，不能混作技能收益。
